note: Friday 16 Oct 2026, 07:02 SGT -- before Asia's open (SGX 09:00, HKEX 09:30). Thursday 15 Oct's US cash close is the latest completed session, a sharp reversal/relief rally after Wednesday's hot-CPI selloff: S&P +0.33% to 7744.06, Nasdaq +0.08%, Dow +1.08%, Russell2000 +1.38%, VIX -2.43% to 16.46. Thursday's own data was genuinely mixed -- core PPI and headline retail sales both ran hotter than consensus (core PPI's fastest monthly rise in ~5 months; retail sales +0.8% vs +0.3% expected, though ex-gas retail sales rose only +0.2%), while Philly Fed manufacturing cooled sharply to 20.9 from 37.8 -- yet several Fed officials (Daly, Bowman, Williams) publicly pushed back on an Oct 27-28 hike despite the hot CPI/PPI prints, and the 10-year yield retreated from an intraday ~5.3% peak to ~5.08-5.09%, pulling the dollar off an 18-month high. Today's swing events are BOE Governor Bailey's (10:00 SGT) and Fed Chair Warsh's (11:30 SGT) Bangkok IMF remarks -- the first public Fed commentary since the hot CPI, watched for any Oct 27-28 hike-urgency signal.

macro.regime: Hawkish-pause relief rally inside an energy-driven stagflation scare
macro.narrative: Friday 16 Oct 2026, 07:02 SGT: Wednesday's hot September CPI (3.7% y/y headline, 2.6% core) and Thursday's even hotter PPI (core PPI's fastest monthly rise in five months) initially spiked Oct 27-28 FOMC hike odds, but Fed officials Daly, Bowman and Williams publicly argued for patience, Philly Fed manufacturing cooled sharply (20.9 vs 30 consensus, down from 37.8), and the 10-year yield retreated from an intraday ~5.3% peak to ~5.08-5.09%, pulling the dollar down from an 18-month high and lifting both equities and metals simultaneously Thursday (S&P +0.33%, GLD +1.79%, SLV +3.39%, GDX +4.34%). A second, AI-specific relief wave hit as Nvidia's Jensen Huang publicly defended CoreWeave's balance sheet, reversing a chip-sector selloff that had erased over $1tn of AI/semiconductor market cap on the week (Korea's Kospi -7.6%, Samsung -9.5%, SK Hynix -11%, spilling into SMIC -3.96%). Underneath the rally, inflation is still substantially energy-driven -- the 2026 Iran war has disrupted the Strait of Hormuz and pushed US diesel above $6/gal -- meaning Thursday's 'good' data (soft Philly Fed, ex-gas retail sales of only +0.2%) is really evidence of a squeezed consumer, not a cooling economy. Credit is sending a split signal: broad HY OAS (~3.16%) is calm, but CCC-rated and AI-adjacent credit (CoreWeave bonds near 15% yield) is flashing stress. Into Friday, markets are focused on BOE Governor Bailey's (10:00 SGT) and Fed Chair Warsh's (11:30 SGT) Bangkok IMF remarks -- the first public Fed commentary since the hot CPI -- for any tightening-urgency signal ahead of the Oct 27-28 FOMC.
